title: What does XLS-81 specify for Permissioned DEX?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-81 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-81 applies permissioned-domain eligibility to decentralized-exchange trading. [1]

Permissioned trading depends on the domain's credential rules and the relevant order and payment behavior. Domain membership does not guarantee a favorable price, adequate liquidity or commercial suitability. Review the exact domain and the network's supported amendments before preparing orders. An open-market offer and a domain-constrained offer need distinct interpretation even when both involve the same asset pair. [1]

A published XLS document describes a design and its constraints; it is not by itself evidence that every network has enabled the corresponding amendment. Read the proposal status, dependencies and current network configuration together. Mainnet, Testnet and development networks can differ, and later fixes can change operational behavior. The source for XLS-81 was fetched directly from the public standards repository. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Final. [1] Author interpretation: use XLS-81 as a specification reference and verify the actual network capability before promising it to a customer. Keep documented design, local tests and validated transactions separate when describing evidence. This article explains the standard rather than claiming a new live deployment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
